area: opening a folder (FolderPicker click -> IPC -> main openRepository -> renderer tree paint)

WHAT REGRESSED: at 7371c4e and every commit before it, src/main/repository.ts open() ended with `return this.refresh()` and refresh() ran only TWO spawns (ls-files --cached + status). The IPC took ~100ms and returned the COMPLETE tree, branch, statuses and the correct workspace view. Commit e18053e (the most recent, 'feat: perf improvements') did two things at once: it added the third `ls-files --others --ignored` spawn to refresh() (repository.ts diff, +GIT_IGNORED_EXCLUSION_PATHSPECS) and it changed open() to return listRootSnapshot() with the real refresh moved behind a fire-and-forget #refreshAndPublish (repositorySessions.ts diff, +setImmediate / +void this.#refreshAndPublish). Net effect on the user-visible metric (time until the folder is usable): 100ms -> 3451ms, a 35x regression, even though the IPC round trip itself got 5x faster.

findings.title: refresh() spends 3.45s in `git ls-files --others --ignored` with 54 exclude pathspecs; pathspecs filter output but git still walks node_modules/.venv
findings.mechanism: `:(exclude,glob)node_modules/**` is applied by git AFTER dir.c has already recursed into and lstat'd every entry of every ignored directory. On materialsx-core-3 that is ~370k ignored paths walked to emit 405. It sits inside the Promise.all at repository.ts:1341, so EVERY refresh -- open, restore, watcher tick, post-save, post-commit -- takes at least that long. Measured 1.85s user + 1.48s sys, i.e. roughly one saturated core per refresh, competing with the renderer during startup and with any other repo session's refresh.
findings.evidence: Measured directly: `git -C materialsx-core-3 ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z -- . <54 pathspecs>` => 3340ms wall / 1.85s user / 1.48s sys / 405 paths. Same command with no pathspecs: 2560ms / 369122 paths. RepositoryService.refresh() end to end: 3556ms cold, 3520ms warm (never gets faster). `ls-files --cached` in the same Promise.all: 17ms. `status --porcelain=v2 -uall`: 45ms. On ~/Developer/vibes/imux refresh() is 153ms cold / 80ms warm; on better-code-diff the ignored walk alone is 438ms. Introduced by e18053e: `git show e18053e~1:src/main/repository.ts` refresh() has only two spawns.
findings.fix:
Replace the single spawn at repository.ts:1344-1353 with a two-phase listing.
Phase 1: `this.#git(['ls-files','--others','--ignored','--exclude-standard','--directory','--no-empty-directory','-z'])`. `--directory` makes git stop at the first ignored directory instead of recursing, so it never enters node_modules/.venv at all.
Phase 2: split the result on trailing '/'. Plain entries are ignored FILES -- keep them. Directory entries whose path contains any segment in EXCLUDED_DIRECTORY_SET (repository.ts:302) are dropped outright (they are exactly what mergeVisiblePaths would have filtered anyway). Feed the surviving directories back as a pathspec list: `this.#git(['ls-files','--others','--ignored','--exclude-standard','-z','--', ...keptDirs])`. Concatenate phase-1 files with phase-2 paths and pass the result to #visiblePaths() unchanged; mergeVisiblePaths' existing isExcludedIgnoredPath (repository.ts:581-585) already strips the few extra .pyc/__pycache__ entries this admits.
Verified equivalent: on materialsx-core-3 the two-phase result is an exact superset of today's 405 paths (416 vs 405; the 11 extras are __pycache__/*.pyc that isExcludedIgnoredPath already rejects); on imux and better-code-diff the sets are byte-identical.
Also cap phase 2: if keptDirs.length > ~32, keep only the first 32 and skip the rest -- a repo with hundreds of non-excluded ignored dirs should degrade to 'some ignored files missing', not to a 3-second stall.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 3385ms on materialsx-core-3 (3451 -> 66); 402ms on better-code-diff (438 -> 36); ~13ms on imux (90 -> 77). Applies to every refresh, so it also removes the same 3.4s from startup restore, every watcher tick and every post-save status update.

findings.title: open() returns a 2-level 400-path readdir skeleton instead of the real tree; the usable tree arrives 3.4s later on a fire-and-forget refresh
findings.mechanism: listRootSnapshot readdirSyncs the root plus one level of each non-skipped top-level directory, skips every dot-prefixed entry, and stops at 400 paths. On a monorepo whose code lives under apps/*/src it produces 84 paths of top-level noise, no branch, no head and no statuses. repositorySessions.open() then returns that as the IPC result and starts the real refresh with `void`, so the renderer paints a skeleton, mounts the tree, computes selection and workspace view from status-less data, and repeats all of it 3.4s later when the real snapshot publishes. The IPC got 5x faster (100ms -> 21ms) while the user-visible 'folder is open' moment got 35x slower.
findings.evidence: Measured with a harness that drives RepositorySessionRegistry.open() directly: materialsx-core-3 -> `(a) IPC returns at 21ms -> paths=84 statuses=0 branch=null` then `publish @3451ms paths=3026 statuses=12 branch=dev changed=2943`. imux -> 21ms / 13 paths, then 126ms / 6245 paths. Before e18053e, `git show 7371c4e:src/main/repository.ts:1209-1219` shows `async open(...) { ...; return this.refresh() }` returning the complete snapshot.
findings.fix:
After FO-1 lands, refresh() costs ~70-130ms, so the skeleton stage is no longer worth its cost. In repositorySessions.ts:128-158, replace the unconditional skeleton return with a deadline race:
  const skeleton = await repository.open(selectedRoot)      // still ~20ms, keeps root/kind detection
  const live = repository.refresh()                          // start it immediately
  const settled = await Promise.race([live, delay(150).then(() => null)])
  ... register the session, start the watcher ...
  if (settled != null) return settled                        // common case: full tree, correct branch/statuses
  void live.then(publish)                                    // slow repo: fall back to the skeleton + publish later
  return skeleton
Keep #refreshAndPublish for the fallback branch only, so the fast path publishes nothing redundant. Also give listRootSnapshot a better skeleton for the fallback: include dot-directories other than .git and descend to depth 3, so the placeholder resembles the real tree.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 3.3s of perceived latency on a large repo (usable tree at ~130ms instead of 3451ms); ~0ms regression for repos where refresh is already under 150ms, and no regression for pathological repos because of the deadline.

findings.title: Workspace view and initial selection are derived from the status-less skeleton and never recomputed, so a dirty repo opens into an empty single-file view and stays there
findings.mechanism: automaticWorkspaceView returns 'multi' only when snapshot.statuses.length > 0 (workspaceMode.ts:14). The snapshot returned by open() after e18053e always has statuses: [] (repository.ts:1318 -> workspaceListing.ts:80), so the answer is always 'file'. firstOpenPathForSnapshot (workspaceMode.ts:43-50) likewise returns null for a git snapshot with no statuses, so App.tsx:703 leaves selectedPath null and the editor is blank. When the real snapshot lands 3.4s later, App.tsx:870 handleRepositoryChange -> applySnapshot fixes selectedPath but nothing re-runs automaticWorkspaceView -- grep confirms its only call sites are the four explicit user actions in App.tsx and three in useGitWorkflow.ts. The user opens a repo with 12 changed files and lands on an empty single-file surface; that reads as 'the app didn't open the folder'. It also loads the wrong lazy chunk: changeWorkspaceView('file') preloads DiffSurface (33KB) when MultiFileReview (103KB) is what will be needed.
findings.evidence: Read App.tsx:825-841 and 843-859; workspaceMode.ts:10-17 and 43-50; measured open() snapshot for materialsx-core-3 = `statuses=0 branch=null`, while the real snapshot 3451ms later = `statuses=12 branch=dev`. `grep -rn automaticWorkspaceView src/renderer/src/` shows no call from handleRepositoryChange or applySnapshot.
findings.fix: Two options, both small. (a) Preferred, and free once FO-2 lands: open() returns a snapshot that already has statuses, so the existing call sites compute the right view. (b) Belt and braces regardless: in App.tsx, track the root whose view has not yet been decided (a ref set in openPickedFolder/openRecentFolder/openFolder), and in handleRepositoryChange (App.tsx:870-890), when change.snapshot.root matches that ref and change.snapshot.statuses is present, call changeWorkspaceView(automaticWorkspaceView(nextSnapshot, null)) once and clear the ref. Mirror the same fix into useReviewWorlds.ts:680-686, which seeds navigationRef with the same wrong view.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Not latency: correctness. Removes one wrong-chunk dynamic import (~103KB parsed later instead of concurrently) and removes the '3.4s of blank editor then the wrong surface' experience.

findings.title: RepositoryService.refresh() has no in-flight dedupe; open, startup restore and the watcher can each run the 3.4s walk concurrently
findings.line: 1334-1372 (no pending-promise guard); callers at src/main/repositorySessions.ts:93, :146, :203, src/main/repositoryWatcher.ts:305, src/main/index.ts:711 and :968, src/main/repository.ts:1553
findings.mechanism: getComparison memoizes its in-flight promise (repository.ts:1433-1444) but refresh() does not. RepositoryWatcher has a private #refreshing flag (repositoryWatcher.ts:297) that only serialises the watcher against itself -- it knows nothing about #refreshAndPublish or startLiveRefresh. Concrete overlap: app launches, index.ts:1007 beginSessionRestore -> index.ts:968 startLiveRefresh starts a 3.4s refresh; the user immediately picks the same folder in the picker; index.ts:481 takes the cached branch and index.ts:493 fires refreshActive() -> a second concurrent 3.4s refresh on the same repo. Each refresh forks three git processes.
findings.evidence: grep for `pendingRefresh|#refreshing|inflightRefresh` in repository.ts returns nothing. Measured contention: one ignored-ls-files 3380ms; two concurrent on the same repo 3797ms; three concurrent 4005ms -- so the wall clock barely degrades but each one burns a core, and the redundant ones deliver identical data.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Removes one full duplicate 3.4s walk (post-FO-1: one duplicate ~70ms walk) plus ~1 core-second of CPU on the launch-then-open-same-folder sequence.

findings.title: Opening a folder never releases the previous repository session; sessions, recursive watchers and refresh loops accumulate for the life of the app
findings.line: 243-262 (insertContentWorld appends), 676-693 (openDeskWorld), 778-784 (onReleaseRepository only from closeWorld); src/main/repositorySessions.ts:113-159 (open never releases), :193-198 (#setActiveRoot only trims caches)
findings.mechanism: openWorkingTree -> openDeskWorld -> dispatch('open-desk') -> insertContentWorld pushes a new desk world; the previous root's world stays in the strip and its main-process session stays in #sessions. releaseRepository is reached only from closeWorld (useReviewWorlds.ts:778-784), i.e. only when the user explicitly closes the tab. So after opening three repos there are three RepositoryService instances, three recursive FSEvents watchers, and three independent watcher flush loops -- and with FO-1 unfixed each of those flushes costs 3.4s of one core whenever anything changes in that tree. That is the mechanism behind 'janky and slow all over the place' after a few folder switches. #setActiveRoot (repositorySessions.ts:193-198) only calls trimCaches on the inactive ones; it does not suspend their watchers.
findings.evidence: Read useReviewWorlds.ts:243-262 (no removal of a same-source desk world for a different root) and :758-786 (release only inside closeWorld). repositorySessions.ts:113-159 contains no this.release(...) call. RepositoryWatcher.setSuspended exists (repositoryWatcher.ts:215-224) and repositorySessions.setSuspended (repositorySessions.ts:174-177) applies it to ALL sessions at once, so there is no per-session suspend for background roots today.
findings.fix:
Two independent changes, do both.
(1) Main: give RepositorySessionRegistry a background policy. In #setActiveRoot (repositorySessions.ts:193), call `watcher.setSuspended(true)` for every session whose root !== root and `setSuspended(false)` for the active one (RepositoryWatcher already re-schedules pending paths on resume, repositoryWatcher.ts:221-223). Track a per-session suspended flag so the global setSuspended from window blur still wins.
(2) Main: cap the session map. In repositorySessions.open(), after inserting, if #sessions.size > 4, release the least-recently-activated session that is not #activeRoot (keep an LRU timestamp updated in #setActiveRoot). The renderer's world strip already tolerates a released root because focusWorld -> activateWorld (useReviewWorlds.ts:595-612) re-opens via onActivateRepository.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Eliminates N-1 concurrent 3.4s (post-fix ~70ms) refresh loops plus N-1 recursive watchers after N folder opens. On the user's workflow (2-3 big repos open) this is the difference between one core of background git and three.

findings.title: The persisted workspace cache is a single slot keyed on lastRoot, so alternating between two repos always takes the slow path
findings.line: 481-496 (openRepository cached branch), src/shared/workspaceCache.ts:16-24 (WorkspaceCache has one lastRoot), :173-191 (mergeWorkspaceCache overwrites lastRoot)
findings.mechanism: openRepository takes the instant hydrate path only when rootsMatch(workspaceCache.lastRoot, resolved). mergeWorkspaceCache sets lastRoot to whichever snapshot was persisted last, so opening B evicts A's cached tree. Open A, open B, come back to A -> A is no longer cached, so A gets the skeleton + slow refresh path all over again. Within one app session repositorySessions.#sessions covers this (repositorySessions.ts:115-126 returns the live snapshot instantly), but across restarts and after FO-5's session cap it does not.
findings.evidence: Read index.ts:481-483 and shared/workspaceCache.ts:173-191. The live file /Users/fuadnafiz98/Library/Application Support/Horus/last-workspace.json holds exactly one root (materialsx-core-3, 3026 paths, 198KB). Cost of the cache machinery itself is negligible and is NOT a problem: measured parseWorkspaceCache 1.3ms at 3026 paths, mergeWorkspaceCache 0.2ms, workspaceCacheBytes 0.1ms; even at a synthetic 20000 paths / 1.75MB it is mergeWorkspaceCache 1.6ms + workspaceCacheBytes 0.7ms + JSON.stringify 0.5ms.
findings.fix: Change WorkspaceCache to `{ version, lastRoot, roots: Record<string, { snapshot, selectedPath, workspaceView, fileText, savedAt }> }`, keep lastRoot only to decide what to restore at launch, and cap `roots` at ~6 entries evicted by savedAt. Apply MAX_WORKSPACE_CACHE_BYTES across the whole file in capWorkspaceCache and shed whole non-lastRoot entries first, then fileText, then paths. openRepository (index.ts:481) then looks up `workspaceCache.roots[resolved]` instead of comparing lastRoot. Bump WORKSPACE_CACHE_VERSION to 2 so the old single-slot file is discarded rather than mis-parsed (parseWorkspaceCache already returns null on a version mismatch, shared/workspaceCache.ts:49).
findings.estimatedGainMs: Makes every repeat open of a recently used repo paint the real tree at ~25ms instead of skeleton+refresh. Post-FO-1 that is ~100ms saved per alternation and, more importantly, removes the skeleton flash entirely.

findings.title: The two-stage snapshot makes the explorer reset and collapse-walk its whole directory list twice per folder open, inside a layout effect
findings.line: 524-554 (useTreeContentSync), 538-547 (collapse every directory then expand changed ones), 1180 (getDirectoryPaths), 1261 (call site); src/renderer/src/WorkspaceRoot.tsx:18 (key={workspaceKey} remount)
findings.mechanism: treeContentSyncMode returns 'reset' whenever the paths array identity changes (treeExpansion.ts:30-38). Because open() delivers 84 paths and the refresh delivers 3026, the effect runs twice: model.resetPaths + model.setGitStatus + a loop calling model.getItem(dir).collapse() over every directory in reverse, then expand for changed dirs. It runs in useLayoutEffect, so it is synchronous before paint. The tree is also fully remounted first, because WorkspaceRoot keys RepositoryWorkspace on snapshot.root.
findings.evidence: Read RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:511-554 and WorkspaceRoot.tsx:11-21. Measured input sizes for the collapse walk on materialsx-core-3: getDirectoryPaths yields 524 directories from 2621 paths in 1.4ms; the pure helpers are cheap (createFileSearchIndex 0.4ms, orderPathsForTree/prepareFileTreeInput 4.3ms) -- the cost is the 524 model.getItem+collapse round trips into @pierre/trees, paid twice. I could not measure the @pierre/trees model mutation cost headlessly (it needs a DOM), so the per-item cost is unquantified.
findings.fix: Primary fix is FO-2: with one snapshot instead of two, the reset happens once. In addition, skip the collapse/expand pass when the previous applied paths array was empty (appliedTreeContentRef.current == null), since a freshly reset model starts collapsed anyway -- guard RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:538-547 with `if (applied != null)`. That removes 524 no-op collapse calls on every first paint of a repo.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Unquantified (needs a DOM harness); removes one full 524-item collapse walk plus one resetPaths per folder open, both on the layout-effect critical path.

findings.title: No progress affordance for the whole open: the picker closes immediately and openingRecentPath is not wired to the chrome button
findings.line: 414-417 (closeFolderPicker before the await), 407 (opening={view.opening}), 785/799 (only openFolder sets `opening`), 827/839 and 845/857 (openPickedFolder/openRecentFolder set openingRecentPath instead)
findings.mechanism: FolderChromeButton renders its spinner from `opening` (FolderPicker.tsx:44,50) and the per-row spinner from `openingPath` (FolderPicker.tsx:117,275). Picking a folder closes the picker first, so the row spinner is unmounted, and `opening` is only ever true for the native-dialog path. For the 3.4s the tree is being fetched the chrome shows a plain folder icon and the workspace shows a skeleton tree with a blank editor -- indistinguishable from a finished open of an almost-empty repo.
findings.fix: Pass `opening={view.opening || view.openingRecentPath != null}` at App.tsx:407 so the chrome button spins for every open path. Better: keep the picker mounted until the promise settles -- move closeFolderPicker into the `finally` of openPickedFolder/openRecentFolder instead of the onSelect handler at App.tsx:415, so the row keeps its per-row spinner (FolderPicker.tsx:275 already supports it) and the list stays disabled via `busy` (FolderPicker.tsx:180).
findings.estimatedGainMs: 0ms real; removes the perception that nothing happened, which is a large part of 'takes ages'.

findings.title: The first folder open from Welcome pulls ~1.34MB of renderer JS before the workspace can mount
findings.mechanism: ensureWorkspaceRoot() at App.tsx:826 starts the import at click time (good -- it overlaps the IPC), but WorkspaceRoot's chunk drags two large shared chunks with it. Rollup names shared chunks after an arbitrary member module, which is why they are called BackToTopButton-*.js and copyFilePath-*.js. Until they parse, App.tsx:488 renders the null branch instead of the workspace.
findings.evidence: out/renderer/assets: WorkspaceRoot-DzrbT5iL.js 268669 B, BackToTopButton-C2hfwQQH.js 611171 B, copyFilePath-C07D3-Xy.js 301887 B, index-Dt3V0rF5.js 155647 B, MultiFileReview-B7hs9zS1.js 103345 B, DiffSurface-CZ_ezeN4.js 33590 B, boot-B2rRKoKF.js 439332 B. Only relevant to the FIRST open of a session; after that the module store (workspaceBoot.ts:22-23) returns the cached component synchronously.
findings.fix: Add an explicit manualChunks entry in electron.vite.config.ts renderer.build.rollupOptions.output so the shared vendor chunk is named and auditable, then run `bunx source-map-explorer out/renderer/assets/BackToTopButton-*.js out/renderer/assets/BackToTopButton-*.js.map` to see what 611KB actually is -- the hidden sourcemaps are already emitted (electron.vite.config.ts:229). Likely candidates to split out of the workspace critical path: @pierre/diffs' highlighter, the terminal, the agent panel. Separately, warm the workspace chunk on picker OPEN rather than on row click: FolderPicker.tsx:42 already calls preloadFolderCatalog on hover/focus, so add preloadWorkspaceRoot() next to it.
findings.estimatedGainMs: First open of a session only; unmeasured here, but 1.34MB of ES-module parse is typically 60-150ms on this class of machine. Preloading on picker open moves all of it off the click.

findings.title: listRootSnapshot's skeleton is actively misleading: dot-directories dropped, depth 2, 400-path cap
findings.mechanism: For a monorepo the useful files live at depth 3+ under apps/*/src, so the skeleton shows 84 unrelated top-level files. The reader then watches the tree change out from under them when the real snapshot lands. Cost of the walk itself is not the problem -- it is 0.4ms on materialsx-core-3 and 2.4ms on imux -- the problem is that the content is not a useful preview.
findings.evidence: Measured listRootSnapshot: 0.4ms / 84 paths on materialsx-core-3, 2.4ms / 13 paths on imux, 0 paths on a plain copied src/ tree. Compare with the real snapshots: 3026 and 6245 paths.
findings.fix: Once FO-2 makes the skeleton a rare fallback, either delete the intermediate paint entirely (return the previous cached snapshot for that root if FO-6 lands, otherwise an explicit loading state) or widen it: allow dot-directories other than .git/.horus, descend to depth 3, raise the cap to 2000. It runs synchronously on the main thread, so measure before raising the cap -- at 2000 paths and depth 3 it will be a few ms, still acceptable, but it must stay bounded.

findings.title: The same folder path is resolved four times per open
findings.line: 478 (resolveExistingRoot -> realpathSync), src/main/folderIndex.ts:70 (realpath in resolveOpenableFolder), src/main/repositorySessions.ts:114 (realpath), src/main/repository.ts:1310 (realpath)
findings.mechanism: openPickedFolder resolves the path in resolveOpenableFolder, openRepository resolves it again synchronously, repositorySessions.open resolves it a third time, RepositoryService.open a fourth. resolveOpenableFolder additionally realpaths the home directory, all 6 DEFAULT_SCAN_ROOT_NAMES and every approvedRoot on each call (folderIndex.ts:78-83). fs.promises.realpath/stat run on the libuv threadpool (default size 4), so a burst of them does serialise against each other and against any other async fs work in main.
findings.evidence: Measured resolveOpenableFolder end to end at 0.4ms with 6 approved roots; fs.promises.realpath 0.1-0.2ms; resolveExistingRoot (sync) 0.1-0.4ms. Total ~1ms -- real but negligible today. It becomes relevant only if approvedRoots grows large or a root is on a network volume.
findings.fix: Have openPickedFolder/openPath pass the already-resolved path down and drop the realpath at repositorySessions.ts:114 and repository.ts:1310 (accept a pre-resolved root). Memoise the home + scan-root realpaths in FolderIndex (it already caches the folder list for 30s, folderIndex.ts:31) instead of recomputing them per resolveOpenableFolder call.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~1ms today; guards against a pathological case on network volumes.

findings.title: Not a bottleneck (measured, so it is not re-investigated): watcher start/stop, runCommand queuing, workspace-cache serialisation, folder-candidate walk, renderer path transforms
findings.mechanism: Recorded so the implementer does not chase them. fs.watch recursive on macOS is FSEvents and costs microseconds. runCommand is a bare execFile with no queue, so the previous repo's 3.4s walk does NOT delay the new repo's rev-parse (verified: rev-parse completed in 39ms while another git walk was running). The workspace cache's JSON work is sub-millisecond. The folder catalog walk is ~20-30ms and cached for 30s. The renderer's pure path transforms are single-digit milliseconds.
findings.evidence: fs.watch({recursive:true}) on materialsx-core-3: start 0.51-2.59ms, close 0.24-0.64ms (measured under both bun and node). collectFolderCandidates: 21ms / 31ms / 18ms across three runs, 103 folders. parseWorkspaceCache 1.3ms; mergeWorkspaceCache 0.2ms (1.6ms at 20k paths); workspaceCacheBytes 0.1ms (0.7ms at 20k). createFileSearchIndex 0.4ms / 2621 paths; getDirectoryPaths 1.4ms -> 524 dirs; orderPathsForTree 4.3ms. gitCommands.ts:255 contains no semaphore or queue.

openQuestions: The @pierre/trees model.resetPaths + per-directory collapse cost (FO-7) could not be measured headlessly — it needs a DOM. Someone should profile one folder open in the packaged app's DevTools performance panel to see how much of the post-snapshot frame is inside useTreeContentSync (RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:524-554) versus React reconciliation.

What is actually inside the 611KB BackToTopButton-*.js and 302KB copyFilePath-*.js shared chunks? The hidden sourcemaps exist next to them; source-map-explorer would settle whether the workspace critical path can be cut. I did not run it because it belongs to the startup reviewer's area.

Does the two-phase ignored listing behave on a repo with a very deep or very wide set of NON-excluded ignored directories (e.g. a repo that gitignores a large data/ tree)? On imux phase 2 was 57ms for .build/ with 4205 files. The proposed cap of ~32 kept directories is a guess; it needs one adversarial repo to calibrate.

Is the ignored-file list (added in e18053e) actually wanted in the explorer at all? If the requirement is really 'show ignored files that are not build output', a much cheaper rule is: phase 1 only (--directory), show the ignored FILES it returns, and render surviving ignored DIRECTORIES as lazy-expandable nodes enumerated only on expand. That makes the ignored side cost ~47ms flat regardless of repo shape.

FO-4's dedupe needs a decision on the mutation-ordering caveat (switchBranch / pullCurrentBranch / checkoutPullRequest call refresh() expecting to observe their own write). A mutation counter is the safe design but adds state; confirm with whoever owns those flows.

scripts/benchmark-startup.mjs failed with 'The restored explorer and review surface did not become usable' within 6s. Given (b)+(c) measured at 3451ms for materialsx-core-3 plus renderer boot, that failure is consistent with the FO-1 stall rather than with missing selectors — worth re-running the benchmark after FO-1 before anyone edits its selectors.
